title: Data Trees
objective: Turn two lists into a grid of points, curve every row, and loft a wave surface.
learn: Branches and data matching: Graft splits lists apart, Flatten brings them back together.

nodes.need: a component that puts every X value on its own branch
nodes.hint: Sets › Tree. One item per branch: {0}, {1}, {2} …
nodes.correct: Graft puts each X value on its own branch. Construct Point now pairs every branch with the WHOLE Y list — a full grid, one row of points per branch.

wrong.flatten: Flatten removes branches — the opposite of what we need. Our list is already flat.
wrong.flipMatrix: Flip Matrix swaps rows and columns of an existing tree; our data is still a flat list.
wrong.reverseList: Reverse List only changes the order.
wrong.shiftList: Shift List offsets items but keeps one flat list.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that puts every X value on its own branch.

nodes.need: a component that combines X, Y and Z values into points
nodes.correct: Construct Point pairs X, Y and Z item by item. Two flat lists of different lengths use “longest list” matching — so you get ONE diagonal row, not a grid. Next, fix that with a tree.

wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter only stores points.
wrong.vector2pt: Vector 2Pt makes vectors from existing points.
wrong.unitZ: Unit Z makes vectors, not points.
wrong.xyPlane: XY Plane makes a plane from an origin point.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that combines X, Y and Z values into points.

nodes.need: a component that draws a smooth curve through each row of points
nodes.hint: Curve › Spline. Smooth, passing through the points.
nodes.correct: Interpolate runs once per branch: each branch of points becomes its own smooth curve.

wrong.line: Line would join points in pairs, giving straight segments.
wrong.polygon: Polygon draws a regular shape from a radius, ignoring the points.
wrong.divideCurve: Divide Curve needs a curve — we’re trying to make one.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that draws a smooth curve through each row of points.

nodes.need: a component that gathers the branch curves into one list
nodes.hint: Sets › Tree. Loft wants all its curves in a single list.
nodes.correct: Each curve sits on its own branch, and Loft works per branch — it would try to loft each curve alone. Flatten collects every curve into one list so Loft can skin through all of them.

wrong.graft: Graft adds even more branches — each curve is already alone.
wrong.reverseList: Reverse List flips order within each branch; the curves stay separated.
wrong.shiftList: Shift List works within each branch; the curves stay separated.
wrong.sortList: Sort List reorders but keeps the branches.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that gathers the branch curves into one list.

nodes.need: a component that skins a surface through the curves
nodes.correct: Loft skins a surface through the curves in order. Graft → operate per branch → Flatten is a pattern you’ll use constantly.

wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces needs closed planar outlines — these curves are open and wavy.
wrong.extrude: Extrude pushes each curve into a ribbon — not one continuous surface.
wrong.pipe: Pipe makes a tube around each curve.
wrong.interpolate: Interpolate is already making the curves.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that skins a surface through the curves.

check.prompt: Which input of Interpolate receives the points?
check.hint: Points that a curve passes through are called its vertices.
check.correct: V is Vertices — the points the curve must pass through.

wrong.D: D is the curve degree (a whole number, usually 3).
wrong.P: P is Periodic — a True/False for closed curves.
wrong.K: K is the knot style — an integer setting.
